what: Work cover photos stack one per screen, full bleed. A wheel, a key, or one click on the right dots advances to the next with a .9s ease (wraps from the end back to the start). During the move, the leaving slide’s photo is pushed out 60% later than its frame, and the entering photo follows from -60% into place, so the layers feel deep. .6s after a slide settles, the work name at bottom left turns on over .3s. Clicking the name pulls that slide up 30% (.6s, starting after .3s) and shrinks the photo to .6x (.3s), then moves on to that work

options.depth: How far the photo lags behind (%), default 60
options.ease: Flip curve (CSS curve text), default ease
options.loop: If off, it does not loop from the end back to the start, default loops
options.dots: Off removes the right-side dot guide, default on
options.wide: Sections advance one at a time only at this width (px) and above, default 768 — below that it is just a stacked list (section height is set by the consumer’s css)
options.--fx-fade · --fx-label-delay: Duration and pause for the name lighting up (via style), default .3s · .6s
options.[data-fx-part=label]: Work name row — pressing the a inside makes it drop out with a motion, then goes to that address

note: fullPage.js runs only once per page, so a second plate does not attach. jquery@3.7.1 · fullpage.js@2.9.7 (MIT, _vendor) and jquery.fullpage.min.css are loaded first. In the original (Semplice coverslider), the picture lagging behind is fullPage’s paid parallax extension (type cover · 60%), so it was rebuilt at the same ratio in onLeave. The dot guide (#fp-nav) attaches to body, so set its color in the consuming css.
